definition: A character standing with its centre of gravity directly over its own base of support has no leverage to push or pull a heavy external object; leverage against an external object requires shifting the centre of gravity off that base first (leaning into the push, straightening a back leg), which is what visibly sells the push as real force rather than a light touch.
purpose: Distinguish a pose that merely touches a heavy object from a pose that credibly applies force to one, using the same centre-of-gravity-over-support relationship as balance, applied to an external interaction instead of self-locomotion.
visible_effect: A character standing upright with weight centred over its feet while contacting an object reads as not really pushing; a character leaning its centre of gravity past its base of support, with a straightening back leg driving the motion, reads as genuinely exerting force.
psychological_or_gameplay_effect: Makes a push or pull against a heavy prop read as credible rather than as a character merely standing next to a moving object.
physical_interpretation: The same centre-of-mass-over-base-of-support relationship structural_understanding already names for balance, read here for its directional consequence: force applied to an external object requires the pushing body to be off its own balance point in the direction of the push, not standing neutrally over its support.
use_cases: any pose where a character pushes, pulls, or braces against a heavy or fixed external object
reviewing a push or pull animation for whether the leaning/back-leg relationship a real push requires is actually present
non_use_cases: lifting a free-standing object straight up, where no horizontal leverage is being applied against a fixed point — see object_center_of_gravity_alignment_with_support for that case instead
a light or small object where no visible leverage is expected in the first place
interactions: structural_understanding — the same measured relationship (`ai/pose.js measurePose` balance against a DECLARED support polygon) as that card's balance check, read here for a directional-leverage consequence rather than a stability verdict

weight_transfer_gates_locomotion_onset (W03, video 21) — the same off-the-support-base mechanism that gates self-locomotion there gates leverage against an external object here; one predicts when the character itself starts moving, this one predicts whether a push reads as real force
cadence_representation: Not computed as a push-leverage judgement. `ai/pose.js measurePose`'s `balance` already reports whether the centre-of-mass proxy sits inside a declared support polygon, and a pose where it falls outside the polygon toward the push direction is exactly the geometry this entry describes — but nothing currently reads that specific configuration (centre of mass outside support, in the direction of a declared push target) as a leverage verdict.
control_surface: `compile_pose` / `author_motion` already return `balance` and `centre_of_mass` when support is declared; nothing consumes them for a push-leverage check.
detection_and_measurement_methods: Real, via `ai/pose.js measurePose`: whether the centre-of-mass proxy falls inside or outside a DECLARED support polygon, and on which side, at a given frame (MOT-011). What is not built is reading that specifically as push leverage: it would need the declared support polygon plus a declared push-target direction, and a rule comparing the centre-of-mass offset against that direction — the measurement primitive exists, the interpretation does not.
generation_or_modification_methods: None. No strategy in `ai/plan.js` currently derives a leaning/off-balance pose from a declared push or pull interaction.
failure_modes: posing a character upright and centred while apparently pushing a heavy object, which reads as the object being light or the contact being decorative rather than load-bearing
leaning far past the support base for an object stated to be light, which reads as an unmotivated stumble rather than intentional effort
roblox_considerations: None beyond the shared Motor6D rig/root model already used by `ai/pose.js measurePose`.
examples: presenter, standing with centre of gravity over his feet, states he has "no leverage to really push something heavy" in that pose — video @ 00:50-00:56

presenter shifts centre of gravity off-balance with a straightening back leg: "now I can actually push something heavy... this leg straightening is what's making something go forward" — video @ 01:02-01:11
evidence_status: video: https://youtu.be/0x9f21vFqcE @ 00:40-01:14 — physically demonstrated on camera by the AnimSchool instructor and stated directly in the transcript, not read from a written source; presenter's stated technique, not a citation; experimental until validated
